name: Yeh Kuo-I
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Yeh Kuo-I is the founder and group president of Inventec, which started as a maker of electronic notebooks in 1975.
Inventec has since expanded into other consumer electronic products such as computers and servers, and today employs more than 36,000 people.
Apart from Inventec, Yeh also has stakes in Taiwan-based Win Semiconductors.
His wealth includes stakes held by his wife, his two sons and his two daughters-in-law. His younger son Sam is Inventec's chairman.

name: Suman Munjal
forbes_bio: Suman Munjal is the son of late Brijmohan Lall Munjal, founder of Hero Group, who died in 2015 at age 92.
He is a non-executive director on the board of two-wheeler behemoth Hero MotoCorp, which is run by his younger brother Pawan Munjal and is the family's most valuable asset.
Suman is the chairman of Rockman Industries, which supplies aluminium die castings to Hero MotoCorp.
He set up the auto components division off Rockman in 1995 and started manufacturing motorcycle chains

name: Yu Rong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2023); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Yu Rong chairs Meinian Onehealth Healthcare Holdings, which offers health exams throughout China.
Yu holds a doctor's degree in Chinese medicine from the China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences and an EMBA of China Europe International Business School.
Yu is a director at Shenzhen Rapoo Technology and Beijing Huamei Kangxun Information Technology.

name: Lloyd Blankfein
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Wikidata (2024)
forbes_bio: Lloyd Blankfein was chairman and CEO of financial behemoth Goldman Sachs from 2006 to 2018, when he was succeeded by David Solomon.
Before leading Goldman Sachs, he worked under then-CEO Henry Paulson as the company's president and chief operations officer from 2004 to 2006.
Blankfein first became a partner at the firm in 1988.
Blankfein grew up in the projects in Brooklyn, graduated as a valedictorian from Thomas Jefferson High School before getting history and law degrees from Harvard.
forbes_facts: Blankfein was diagnosed with lymphoma late in 2015, and after months of chemotherapy, he said he was likely cured of the disease.

name: Chin Jong Hwa
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2024); Hurun China (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Chin Jong Hwa is the largest shareholder of Hong Kong-listed auto-parts supplier Minth Group, which he started in 1997.
In 2016, Minth became the first auto-parts maker to receive a permit from China to make electric cars.
Chin stepped down from Minth in 2019. His wife Wei Ching Lien has taken over as chairman and CEO.
Their daughter, Chin Chien Ya, is a non-executive director at Minth. Son William is chief strategy officer and executive director.
Minth owns more than 70 factories globally, and is building new facilities in India and Serbia.
forbes_facts: Chin once worked as a counselor at China Youth Corps, a youth organization in Taiwan.

name: He Xiaopeng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2018-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: He Xiaopeng is the cofounder and chairman of Xpeng, an electric vehicle maker dual-listed in New York and Hong Kong.
German automaker Volkswagen announced in July 2023 it would acquire a 4.99% stake in Xpeng via a $700 million capital increase, and subsequently gain an observer seat on its board.
In August 2023, Xpeng acquired ride-hailing platform Didi's smart-car development arm in a $744 million all-stock deal to be completed in stages, with Didi owning an eventual 3.25% stake.
Before Xpeng, the mogul founded browser UCWeb, which was acquired by Alibaba in 2014.

name: David Mindus
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: David Mindus is the founder and CEO of Swedish commercial real estate company Sagax AB.
Mindus and two partners began buying warehouses and light industrial properties around Stockholm in 2000 after identifying the sector as undervalued.
Mindus owns more than 17 percent of Sagax, which listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange in 2004.
Its portfolio consists of more than 37 million square feet across 673 properties.
Before Sagax, Mindus worked at GE Capital, where he helped found the company's Swedish real estate investment business.

name: Frank Holding Jr
forbes_bio: Frank Holding is Chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a $31 billion (market cap) commercial banking chain, since 2008.
Holding's grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to Frank's father, Lewis Holding.
Today, Frank and his four sisters collectively own about 20% of the bank.
Holding also serves as a board member of Wake Forest University.

name: Alexander Savelyev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Alexander Savelyev is the controlling shareholder Bank of Saint Petersburg, which is among the 20 largest banks in Russia.
He was named CEO of the bank in 2001 and now owns about 27%, while his daughter and top managers control another 28%.
In 2022, while most Russian banks suffered losses, Bank of Saint Petersburg remained profitable.
Prior to entering the banking industry, Savelyev worked in several transport enterprises during the 1980s and 1990s.
The Bank of Saint Petersburg was sanctioned by U.S. Department of Treasury in 2023.
forbes_facts: Russian president Vladimir Putin owns 230 shares of Bank of Saint Petersburg, according to his tax statement.

name: Lin Por-Fong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Lin Por-Fong has been serving as the chairman of Taiwan Glass, one of Asia's largest glass suppliers, since 2009.
The company was founded in 1964 by his late father, Lin Yu-Chia, who took it public nine years later.
It has five plants in Taiwan and 15 in mainland China after expanding into the region in 1993.
Por-Fong's brother Por-Shih is the company's president and CEO; another brother Por-Chun is its executive director.

name: Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes is an heir to a stake in Brazilian industrial conglomerate Votorantim.
His grandfather, Jose Ermirio de Moraes, founded Grupo Votorantim in 1918; in 2021 the group had revenues of about $7 billion.
The group does business in more than 20 countries in the aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, banking, and cement industries.
Jose Roberto inherited an 8% stake in the family-owned company after the death of his father, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Filho, in 2001.
Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes previously appeared on Forbes? list of the World's Billionaires in 2014.
forbes_facts: His two siblings, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Neto and Neide Helena de Moraes also inherited stakes in the family company.

name: George Pedersen
forbes_bio: George Pedersen is the cofounder ManTech International, which he started in 1968 with a single contract with the U.S. Navy.
Today, the defense and intelligence contractor has 8,700 employees and nearly $2.5 billion in revenue.
Pedersen, a Staten Island native, owns a third of the firm, which is based in Virginia's Fairfax County.
ManTech went public on the Nasdaq in February 2002
Pedersen stepped down as CEO in 2017 after a nearly five-decade run; he still serves as chairman.
